# Rules

## Laws (never bypassable)

### `blueprint.dsl` Blueprint DSL shape

Only the keys the Blueprint DSL defines, version 1, at most 6 screens with unique ids, at most 4 short notes, and every goTo names another screen of the document.

### `component.api` Component API

Only real components, with their declared props and allowed values; children only on components that accept them, as a list of nodes.

### `focus.single` One focus per screen

A TV screen has exactly one focused element — the one the viewer is on.

### `frame.layout` Frame 1280×720, margin 32, gutter 16

The layout is 1280×720 with a 32pt safe-area margin the frame applies itself; the root is the layout container and adds no margin; top-level modules and stacked columns sit exactly 16pt apart.

### `grid.8pt` 8pt grid

Every spacing and every grid-bound size is a multiple of 8pt (the documented exceptions aside).

### `layers.stack` Video, overlay, content

Every screen is three layers — video, overlay, content. The content layer is transparent: the outermost container paints no background.

### `layout.anchor-structure` Anchor structure

Only a direct child of the root can be anchored, and never the component that holds a level’s focus in the content.

### `primitives.budget` Primitive budget

At most 3 primitives in a chain (a primitive inside a primitive) and 6 per screen, text included; beyond that the need is a new component — a Proposal.

Applies to: `primitive:Box`, `primitive:Stack`, `primitive:Text`

### `primitives.reuse` A primitive says why no component would do

Every primitive carries "reuse": the registry components it considered, by name, and why none of them expresses the need.

Applies to: `primitive:Box`, `primitive:Stack`, `primitive:Text`

### `tokens.only` Tokens only

A design value is always a token name — never a raw hex, rgb, px, rem or % value.

### `tokens.semantic-tier` Semantic tier, never core

A screen names semantic (or layout) tokens; core tokens exist only for other tokens to point at.

## Patterns (breakable in Exploratory mode, declared)

### `flow.link-roles` Link roles

The main menu carries no link; a back control returns exactly one level; a close control returns to Home.

Applies to: `MainMenu`, `RoundedButton`, `CloseButton`

### `flow.next-level` Links from N to N+1

A link opens the next level or goes back up — it never skips a level.

### `flow.rail-consistency` Rail consistency

A second-level page shows as many interactivity buttons as the Home rail it is entered from.

Applies to: `InteractivityButton`

### `layers.overlay-model` Overlay models

Every screen names one of the fixed layer models, on that model’s level, with its content on the side the model shades.

### `layout.anchor` One anchored group

A frame anchors at most one element group, and only on levels that allow an anchor.

### `layout.no-static-center` No static centering

The master layout is never statically centered — TV layouts follow the focus.

### `layout.root-align` Root with align: stretch

The stack that holds the components always stretches; a module places itself inside it.

### `layout.slots` Slots, order and parents

A component with slots takes each slot at most once, in slot order; a component with parents goes only directly inside them.

Applies to: `ContentCard`, `ContentCardHeader`, `ContentCardBody`, `ContentCardFooter`, `TableCell`

### `level.initial-focus` Where focus starts

Each level starts its focus on its own component: the main menu on Home, an interactivity button on level 2, the rounded or close button on level 3.

Applies to: `MainMenu`, `InteractivityButton`, `CloseButton`, `RoundedButton`

### `level.module-limit` Module limit per level

A navigation level shows at most its number of content modules (one on levels 0, 2 and 3).

### `level.root-direction` Root direction per level

On levels that require it, the outermost container is a column; on levels whose stack sits at the end of the frame, it is justified to the end.

### `registry.new-component` Catalog components only

A screen is built from the catalog; a component the registry lacks is a declared Proposal (a description and its proposed props), never an invented one.

Applies to: `primitive:Box`, `primitive:Stack`, `primitive:Text`, `Proposal`

## Conventions (breaking one only produces a note)

### `copy.button-label` Button labels say what they do

A button label names the action it performs.

Applies to: `Button`, `WideButton`, `InteractivityButton`

### `render.legibility` Legible text

Text never lands on top of other text and is never squeezed to nothing by a container too small for it.

### `templates.reference` Reference screens

A generation starts from the reference screen whose shape the plan describes.

## How to declare

### `@deviation`

Form: `@deviation <ruleId>: <why>`

Breaks a pattern rule on purpose (Exploratory mode). Laws and conventions cannot be declared.

- On a node: `{/* @deviation <ruleId>: <why> */}` right before the element it covers.
- On the screen: A comment on the component (JSDoc or line comments above it); covers the screen.

### `@reuse`

Form: `@reuse <KitComponent>: <why>`

A primitive (Box, Text) says which kit component it considered and why none would do. Required on every primitive.

- On a node: `{/* @reuse <KitComponent>: <why> */}` right before the primitive.
- On the screen: Not applicable: it belongs to one primitive.

### `@proposal`

Form: `@proposal (JSDoc block: why / description / figma / proposedApi)`

A component the kit lacks, written in `components/` of your folder. Each exported component carries the block; why, description and one proposedApi line (`<prop>: "<type>"`) are required, figma is optional.

- On a node: Not applicable: it sits on the component, not on the element that uses it.
- On the screen: A JSDoc block above each exported component in `components/`.

### Where each pattern is declared

- On the node where it breaks (a screen-level declaration is an error): `flow.link-roles`, `flow.next-level`, `layout.slots`, `registry.new-component`
- On the screen, or on the root node: `flow.rail-consistency`, `layers.overlay-model`, `layout.anchor`, `layout.no-static-center`, `layout.root-align`, `level.initial-focus`, `level.module-limit`, `level.root-direction`
